caption: Valorizzare le differenze, non cancellarle.
text: Why do you think these lights are on? Because there is a potential difference between plus and minus. If you don't have this difference, the light would be off. If I take this and I leave it, it's going to fall because of difference of altitude. If you don't have difference, it's not going to fall. It's going to stay fixed. So if we had no differences in the physical world, we would be in a total immobility world. Nothing would move, nothing would leave without differences. So if you try to erase the differences, you are trying to erase life. And in a social world, if you erase differences, you erase the willingness of people to live and to progress. Because if you don't see differences, if you don't see a better world, better way of living, a better way of point of reference, you are not incited to go forward. You're just simply saying, why should I move? Why should I work? Why should I do something if you don't have differences? So erasing the differences, it means making the world immobile, totally immobile. We should enhance differences, which has nothing to view to discriminate people. You discriminate people when you take out their rights, not when you enhance differences. He's blonde, I am brown, he's from Italy, he's from Belgium, he comes from Africa, I come from the North Pole. These are the differences that are normal, and they are not bad and good, they are simply differences. And this is what characterizes our society. Very simple.
